title: Google launches universal Gemini agent with a coworker inbox at Gemini at Work 2026
subtitle: Enterprise customers can now spin up persistent agents with their own Workspace account, Gmail address, calendar, and Drive — and the router dispatches jobs across Gemini and Anthropic's Claude.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google Cloud used its Gemini at Work 2026 event on October 8 to launch a single, universal Gemini agent for enterprise work. Alongside temporary sub-agents that spin up for one-off jobs, businesses can create persistent coworker agents that get their own identity inside the company — a Workspace account with a Gmail address, calendar, and Drive storage. The agent orchestrates across Gemini and Anthropic's Claude, routing each job to the model Google judges best for quality and cost, and reaches into Microsoft 365, Slack, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and any Model Context Protocol server. It is in private preview for enterprise customers, with no public pricing yet.

Treating an agent as a coworker rather than a tool changes the integration surface. Colleagues can CC it, meetings can include it, and it keeps running in the cloud after the laptop closes — so a single task can stretch across hours or days. The multi-model routing is the other signal. Google is openly putting a competitor's model inside its own agent product rather than locking customers to Gemini, which is a different posture from the vertical bundles Microsoft and AWS have pushed this year.

Microsoft, Salesforce, and ServiceNow have each announced persistent agents in the last six months, but Google's version embeds the agent inside the identity fabric most companies already use for humans. The move follows Google's Gemini 4 Argon release in late September and the Nano Banana 2.1 image model's general availability on October 9, extending a run that has pushed Google's enterprise AI story from catching up to defining the agent-as-colleague pattern.

A coworker agent is a probabilistic system wrapped in a corporate account — and corporate accounts have permissions. Before experimenting, learn how your organization scopes access tokens, mailbox rules, and audit logs for the agent's Workspace identity. The difference between a helpful intern and a security incident is the fence around what the account can touch, and the people building that fence are the ones hiring in 2027.
